headline: Recommenced deliveries after supply chain delays tied to Iran conflict and Netherlands export licences; expanding capacity to 200 units/month and adding new Defence Prime customer with international defence sales
reasoning: KTEK had been unable to ship product due to supply chain disruptions caused by the Iran conflict and export licence difficulties out of the Netherlands where some assembly occurs. The company has now resolved these issues through alternative supply routes and new assembly facilities in the US. Monthly manufacturing capacity has been increased to 200 units. A new large Defence Prime customer with international defence department clients has been signed. The company has 5 quarters of cash runway even under a do-nothing scenario, and management describes the underlying business model as nominally profitable with growth investment being the primary use of capital.
quote: We've now worked to come around those problems have alternatives and we're very pleased to be restarting shipping well today... we've also announced expanded capacity. Meanwhile, we are also, we now have the confidence to get more customers... we just announced recently a very large new customer, Defence Prime, which has international defence customers, right. They sell to defence departments. And you know that that's a very large amount of work.
episode_title: KTEK resumes deliveries as defence demand builds

headline: US and European governments investing heavily in drone/unmanned capability; US DoD requesting Congress approve $75 billion earmarked for unmanned systems out of a $1.4 trillion budget
reasoning: Howard Digby highlights the asymmetric battlefield dynamic emerging from recent large conflicts, which has fundamentally changed how militaries view drone capability. Both European governments and the US government are investing heavily in unmanned systems. The US Department of Defense has put forward a $1.4 trillion budget request to Congress, with $75 billion specifically earmarked for unmanned capability — the segment KTEK's customers sell into, representing a very large addressable market.
quote: You've heard all governments are investing heavily, European governments, the US government in, in drone, in, in drone capability. And that's because of the asymmetric battlefield. Things have changed completely. These reasonable big conflicts, recent conflicts have demonstrated that the US Department of War has, has come up with a mass, you know, budget the request for Congress to approve $1.4 trillion. But a very large sort of component of that, a significant component of that $75 billion has been earmarked for unmanned, unmanned capability. So that's our, that's our segment. That's the segment that our customers are selling into.
episode_title: KTEK resumes deliveries as defence demand builds
